 England to face Norway in Nations League quarter-final; Wales to play Slovenia in play-offs
 20 November 2026 Summary
 England have drawn Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, in a repeat of the World Cup quarter-final
 Thomas Tuchel's side could face Belgium or Germany in the semi-finals 
 Wales will face Slovenia in the play-offs to determine promotion/relegation from groups
 In the quarter-finals, each league winner - which includes England - will play their second leg at home 
 In the play-offs, Wales will play their second leg at home, because they are from the higher league
 Close form Your views on the Nations League draw
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Written by Ben Ramsdale, Craig Nelson, Harry Poole & Huzaifah Khan.
 Most recent Most popular Nations League draws published at 12:12 GMT 12:12 GMT 
 England have drawn Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, while Wales will play Slovenia in the Group A/B play-off and the Republic of Ireland will face Croatia. 
 The full Nations League draw, including the quarter-finals and semi-finals, is below, along with the play-offs for Group A/B and Group B/C.
 Nations League quarter-finals :
 Spain v France
 Norway v England 
 Netherlands v Portugal
 Belgium v Germany
 Nations League semi-finals :
 Netherlands/Portugal v Spain/France 
 Belgium/Germany v Norway/ England 
 Group A/B play-offs :
 Bosnia and Herzegovina v Denmark
 Hungary v Serbia
 Republic of Ireland v Croatia
 Slovenia v Wales 
 Group B/C play-offs :
 Cyprus v North Macedonia
 Estonia v Romania
 Faroe Islands v Georgia
 Belarus v Israel

 The only time Wales have faced Slovenia published at 12:08 GMT 12:08 GMT 
 Wales will take on Slovenia for just the second time in their history in the Nations League play-offs in March.
 The last time the two nations faced each other was in August 2005 in a goalless friendly played in Swansea - back when the Swansea.com Stadium was called the White Rock.
 Current boss Craig Bellamy started that day and will hope to get their first win over Slovenia and save Wales' status in Nations League Group A.
 Could this match-up be a bit more memorable?

 Norway's star-studded squad published at 11:57 GMT 11:57 GMT 
 As we know, this is a Norway side littered with quality. 
 England know all about that from the last time they met.
 Norway started well and then grew again as their World Cup quarter-final wore on, before Jude Bellingham's strike decided things.
 So which top talents do Norway have at their disposal?
 Erling Haaland, Man City - 61 caps, 68 goals
 Antonio Nusa, RB Leipzig - 36 caps, 10 goals
 Martin Odegaard, Arsenal - 79 caps, 6 goals
 Andreas Schjelderup, Benfica - 24 caps, 3 goals
 Plus the likes of Oscar Bobb, Alexander Sorloth and Kristoffer Ajer. 
 It won't be easy for England, that's for sure.
 Image source, Getty Images

 England v Norway - head-to-head record published at 11:49 GMT 11:49 GMT 
 This will be the 14th time England have faced Norway and the sixth time they've met in a competitive game.
 England have won eight times
 There have been three draws
 And two Norway wins
 You have to go back to 1993 to find the last Norway win - a 2-0 scoreline in Oslo in a World Cup qualifier - against an England team that featured the likes of Paul Gascoigne, Teddy Sheringham, Carlton Palmer and Lee Dixon. 
 The last England win? That's quite easy. Just over four months ago in the World Cup quarter-finals - a memorable 2-1 victory clinched by an extra-time winner from Jude Bellingham . 
 Image source, Getty Images

 Another country for the Red Wall to tick off published at 11:44 GMT 11:44 GMT 
 Dafydd Pritchard 
BBC Sport Wales 
 Speak to members of the Red Wall - the nickname for Wales' fans - and they'll tell you how excited they get about visiting new countries.
 Well, the men's senior team have never played in Slovenia before, so this is a chance for them to tick off another.
 It's meant to be a beautiful, mountainous place, so Wales should feel right at home.
 Slovenia will pose a tough footballing examination, though.
 They lost only once in their Nations League campaign, away against group winners Switzerland.
 And you might remember they held England to a goalless draw at Euro 2024.
 There are only eight places between Wales (41st) and Slovenia (49th) in the Fifa world rankings too.
 Image source, Getty Images
